## Verification Summary

| Claim | Status | Key Finding |
|---|---|---|
| **C1** — AWS sales +17% YoY in Q1 2024 | ✅ **Supported** | Q1 2024 10-Q (filed 2024-05-01) explicitly states "AWS sales increased 17% in Q1 2024 compared to the comparable prior year period." GAAP, reported actual. |
| **C2** — Q1 2024 operating income was $4.8B | ⚠️ **Conflicted** | The $4.8B figure is Q1 **2023** operating income (the prior-year comparison). Q1 **2024** operating income was actually **$15.3B**. The claim misattributes the period. |
| **C3** — Trainium 70% global inference market share, June 2024 | ❌ **Insufficient** | No SEC primary-source evidence exists for any Trainium market-share figure. This type of claim typically originates from third-party market research, not 10-Q/10-K filings. |

---

## Detailed Reasoning

### C1 — Publish ✅
The claim matches the Q1 2024 10-Q exactly. The reporting period is correct (Q1 2024, ended March 31, 2024), the basis is GAAP, and the figure is a reported actual — not guidance or a forward-looking estimate. The source was filed 2024-05-01, well before the as_of date of 2024-08-02. No friction.

### C2 — Do NOT publish; revise ⚠️
My pre-verification suspicion was confirmed: the anchor text "Operating income increased from $4.8" was describing the *increase from* the prior-year base, not the current-period figure. The actual GAAP operating income for Q1 2024 was **$15.3 billion**, not $4.8 billion. The $4.8B belongs to Q1 2023.

**If the brief needs an operating-income claim, the corrected version would be:**
> "Amazon Q1 2024 operating income was $15.3 billion, up from $4.8 billion in Q1 2023."
— Source: AMZN-2024Q1 10-Q, passage P482.

However, I will not auto-publish the corrected claim without a separate verification pass, per cautious-analyst protocol.

### C3 — Do NOT publish; insufficient ❌
No anchor hits for "Trainium" or "market share" appeared in any of the four available SEC sources. The verifier returned zero evidence passages and flagged missing fields for "Trainium market share," "global inference market share," and "June 2024 data." SEC filings (10-Q, 10-K) generally do not report proprietary chip market-share estimates. This claim would require a third-party market-research source (e.g., IDC, Gartner) that is outside the scope of this SEC-based corpus. Even if such a source existed, "70% of global inference market share" is an extraordinarily strong claim that would need direct citation to the research methodology.
